text:
The man is likely to prevail. When the woman conveyed the house to him, he owned both the dominant and servient parcels, so the easement was extinguished by merger. His later warranty deed to the purchaser didn't mention the easement, so it didn't revive it, and there is no implied easement because the man never used the path while he owned both parcels. I disagree with the team note: recording the original grant doesn't help the purchaser, because the easement no longer existed when the man conveyed the house.

CONFIDENCE: 82
